No relationship line to user. This is a standalone table — Better Auth uses identifier (email string) to match, not a FK. It's for email verification tokens.
every group MUST have a creator (createdBy NOT NULL)
A room is one bill-splitting session. It can be created from a group ('ISE Squad dinner') or standalone ('Quick Split'). finalizedAt is when the host locks the bill and moves to payment stage.
Unlike groupMembers where userId is NOT NULL, here userId IS nullable. A friend can join a room with just a display name — no sign up. lineUserId is stored separately for sending LINE notifications.
A section groups bill items together. Each section can have its own VAT rate, service charge rate, and discount. Thai restaurants typically charge 7% VAT + 10% service charge.
"Each menu item on the receipt. Quantity × unitPrice = item total. Items belong to a room and optionally to a section.
This is the M:N junction table. If 3 people share Pad Thai, there are 3 rows here. The calculation engine divides the item price by the number of splits.
There's a unique constraint on (itemId, memberId) — one person can only claim an item once.

Each non-host member gets one payment row. The amount is their total share including proportional VAT/service charge. Status tracks the payment lifecycle. The slip* columns store transfer slip verification data — when a friend uploads a bank slip, we extract the QR code and verify it against Bank of Thailand records.

When a friend opens the bill page and allows notifications, the browser gives us an endpoint URL + encryption keys. We store one subscription per member per room. p256dh and auth are Web Push encryption keys — required by the VAPID protocol to send encrypted push notifications without Firebase

Prevents duplicate reminders. The scheduler runs every 15 minutes and checks: 'Have I already sent the 30-minute reminder for this payment?' If a row exists with tier='30m' for that payment, skip it. channel tracks whether we sent via LINE or web push.
